source_text: Nemo maculam habens offeret. Maculae vitiorum. Christus immaculatus.
thought_title: The unblemished offerer and Christ's purity
orientation: Origen is applying the Levitical rule about priestly blemishes to the moral life, saying that no one with a blemish may offer, and then identifies Christ as the one without blemish.
pass_a_gloss: No one having a blemish will offer. Blemishes of vices. Christ unblemished.

choices.why: The literal physical blemish of Leviticus, which Origen reads morally as vice; 'blemish' keeps the physical-to-moral transfer visible.
Future tense of the prohibition in the law, kept as future to preserve the legal force.
Echoes macula directly, showing Christ as the negation of the blemish; the glossary's 'holy' is not used because the term is specifically about lack of blemish.

pass_b_english: No one who has a blemish will offer. The blemishes are vices. Christ is unblemished.

last_rejected.quote: No one who has a blemish will offer
last_rejected.why: Future 'will offer' changes command/prohibition to prediction; source is jussive/hortatory.
last_rejected.fix: No one with a blemish may offer, or Let no one with a blemish offer.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'offeret' is future indicative; standard rendering of prohibitions in biblical/paraphrase context. No meaning lost.
